items.problem: Migrated WinUI 3 app builds cleanly but fails package registration (0x80073CF6 / inner 0x80070002 on the windows.capability extension) and never launches, because Package.appxmanifest kept the UWP sample's uap4:CustomCapability 'Microsoft.onDemandHotspotControl_8wekyb3d8bbwe', which needs an SCCD absent for a sideloaded package.
items.evidence: migration-score.json winui_launch_error; discrepancies.md 'Blocker'; results.json runs=false; final Package.appxmanifest <Capabilities> retains <uap4:CustomCapability .../>.
items.skill_search: grep -i 'CustomCapability|custom capability|SCCD|restricted' across skills/winui-uwp-migration (SKILL.md, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, scripts/*.ps1).
items.wrong_text_if_any: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md item 3: 'Keep any UWP <Capability> entries you actually use (e.g. <DeviceCapability Name="webcam" />) but add the runFullTrust line above no matter what.' — no exception for SCCD-gated custom/restricted capabilities.
items.root_cause: The manifest migration checklist and validator cover Windows.Desktop target, rescap namespace, runFullTrust, and windows.backgroundTasks extensions, but never address uap4:CustomCapability or other SCCD-gated capabilities. The agent copied the capability verbatim (item 3 even told it to keep capabilities), and the failure only surfaces at registration time, which the migration agent never reaches.
items.proposed_fix: Add Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 check 5d that FAILs when the manifest declares uap4:CustomCapability (or other SCCD-gated restricted capabilities) and instructs removal; add MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md manifest-checklist item 6 documenting the 0x80073CF6/0x80070002 windows.capability failure and the remove-the-capability fix; extend SKILL.md pre-flight item 5 to name SCCD custom capabilities.
items.generalizes: UWP SDK samples frequently declare uap4:CustomCapability / restricted SCCD-gated capabilities for privileged hardware and enterprise features. Every such sample migrated to a sideloaded WinUI 3 package hits the identical windows.capability registration failure (build clean, launch fatal) until the capability is stripped — the same invisible-at-build, fatal-at-registration class as the existing background-task checklist item.
